a

MP1: In the particle model, an electron absorbs the energy of a single photon. MP2: The photon's energy depends on frequency, not intensity, so is independent of intensity. / The wave model incorrectly predicts depends on intensity.

b

Use of photoelectric equation = hf - hf₀. Substitution: 8.0 × 10⁻²⁰ = (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴)(9.0 × 10¹⁴) - hf₀. Calculation to find f₀ ≈ 7.8 × 10¹⁴ Hz.

The value = 8.0 × 10⁻²⁰ J is taken from the source image, which contradicts the paraphrased text. A correct answer is required to 2 or 3 significant figures.

c

Similarity: The gradient is the same (equal to Planck's constant h). Difference: They have different x-intercepts (threshold frequencies) OR different y-intercepts (work functions).

Award 1 mark for a valid similarity and 1 mark for a valid difference.

d

The increase in wavelength / decrease in frequency of the scattered X-rays.

Allow mention of the dependence of wavelength shift on scattering angle.

question.html:
In an experiment to investigate the photoelectric effect, monochromatic electromagnetic radiation is incident on a metal surface.

When the frequency of radiation is 9.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz, photoelectrons of maximum kinetic energy 8.0 × 10⁻²⁰ J are emitted from the metal surface.

a The maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons does not depend on the intensity of radiation. Explain how this observation supports the particle nature of light. [2]

b Determine the threshold frequency of the metal surface. [3]

c

The variation of the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons is plotted against the frequency of radiation for two surfaces made of different metals.

Identify one similarity and one difference between the graphs obtained.

[2]

d

In the Compton experiment, X-rays are scattered by electrons.

State which feature of this experiment cannot be explained using the wave model of light.

[1]
